metadata.title: Sphinx Quiz System Comprehension
metadata.description: Test your understanding of the Sphinx quiz system architecture and concepts
metadata.author: Claude

questions.prompt: What are the two quiz modes supported by the Sphinx quiz system?
questions.explanation: Sphinx supports two quiz modes: 'static' for fixed question order quizzes, and 'adaptive' which uses Item Response Theory (IRT) to dynamically select questions based on the test-taker's estimated ability level (theta).

questions.prompt: Which of the following are valid question types in the Sphinx quiz system?
questions.explanation: Sphinx supports four question types: multiple-choice (single correct answer), multi-select (multiple correct answers with partial or all-or-nothing scoring), free-text (text input with exact/contains/regex matching), and code-challenge (programming problems with test cases). True-false is not a distinct type - it would be implemented as a multiple-choice question.

questions.prompt: In multi-select questions with partial scoring, what is the formula used to calculate the score? Express your answer in terms of correct selections, incorrect selections, and total correct options.
acceptedAnswers: correct selections - incorrect selections / total correct
questions.explanation: For multi-select questions with partial scoring, the score is calculated as: (correct selections - incorrect selections) / total correct options. The minimum score is 0, so negative results are clamped. A score of 1 (100%) means all correct options were selected with no incorrect selections.
